title: Japan's JCR Upgrades India's Sovereign Credit Rating To A-, Cites Strong Growth And Healthier Financial System
text:
Economy
Swarajya Staff
Sep 03, 2026 | Updated 09:27 AM GMT+5:30
Save & read from anywhere!
Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app.
Japan Credit Rating Agency upgraded India's sovereign credit rating to A- from BBB+ on Tuesday (2 September), raising both foreign currency and local currency long-term issuer ratings whilst maintaining a stable outlook.
The agency also raised India's country ceiling by one notch to A.
JCR stated this was an unsolicited rating, meaning it was issued without a request from the Indian government.
The upgrade reflects India's sustained economic growth of around 7 per cent, driven by strong private consumption and public investment.
Real GDP growth during fiscal year 2026 was recorded at 7.7 per cent.
JCR cited India's solid economic growth, the effectiveness of policies that strengthen foundations for growth, and the improved soundness of the financial system.
The agency highlighted government measures such as digital public infrastructure and the goods and services tax, which have steadily strengthened the country's economic base.
The gross non-performing loan ratio fell to 1.8 per cent at the end of March 2026, helped by the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, government capital support and stronger RBI supervision.
Capital adequacy and profitability remained sound, whilst asset quality also improved in the non-banking financial sector.
However, JCR flagged India's elevated general government debt and fiscal deficits as key structural constraints, noting that India's federal structure, fiscal transfers aimed at reducing disparities between states and the influence of electoral cycles on fiscal management tend to keep deficits elevated.
The agency estimates that the economy could maintain a high growth rate of over 6 per cent in fiscal year 2027.
Last month, two global rating agencies, S&P and Fitch, affirmed India's investment-grade rating, citing a dynamic and fast-growing, robust economy with policy stability and high infrastructure investment.
The upgrade positions India more favourably on JCR's sovereign rating scale, potentially boosting international confidence in the country's financial position and supporting investor sentiment.
